venue.name: Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre
venue.description: The Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre is a marine research and teaching station on the outer west coast of Vancouver Island, governed by the Pacific Marine Science Alliance, a not-for-profit registered Canadian charity. It has run a field trips program since 1975, hosting groups who stay on campus for two, three or four nights and spend their days in the laboratories, out on the boats and along the surrounding beaches and rainforest. Field trips run in the fall, September to November, and in the spring, February to April, on dates set before each season. The rest of the year the campus works as a research station: public access is limited to the main building, there is no public access to the foreshore and docks, and day tours are not offered at present.
venue.address: 100 Pachena Rd, Bamfield, British Columbia, Canada, V0R 1B0

facility_notes.washrooms: Showers and toilets are conveniently located on each floor and are maintained to support regular use by residents. Each floor has 2-4 bathrooms and 2-4 showers. We provide hand soap, toilet paper, and paper towels.
facility_notes.lunch_space: The BMSC dining hall is a peanut-free facility and we are able to accommodate vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, and dairy-free meal options. Meal hours are normally Breakfast 7:30 to 8:00 am, Lunch 12:30 to 1:00 pm, Dinner 6:00 to 6:30 pm.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: If you have any accessibility needs, please reach out to our team to see if our living spaces and surrounding areas can accommodate them.

restrictions: Pets are not permitted on BMSC property.
BMSC has implemented a scent-free workplace environment.
The BMSC dining hall is a peanut-free facility.
There is no public access to our foreshore, docks, and rest of the campus.
Close-toed footwear is required in labs and on boats.
In order to comply with Transport Canada regulations for marine vessel capacity, we require group sizes to be in multiples of 12.
venue.hours_notes: Office Hours: Monday-Friday, 8:30am to 4:30pm (PT). BMSC is a working campus with public access limited to the main building, and tours are not being offered at this time.
venue.seasonal_notes: We offer field trips in the Fall (September to November) and Spring (February to April). Field trips during these months will have pre-set dates, announced by email list and social channels before each season.

programs.name: Marine science field trip, 2 nights and 3 days
programs.description: A residential marine biology field trip on the BMSC campus. The published price includes accommodation, meals, instructional programming, laboratory and classroom facilities, and educational materials, and the site describes it as an estimated cost per person starting at $713. Final pricing is based on group size, accommodation requirements, season, and selected educational activities, and transport to and from Bamfield is not included. Bookings must be in multiples of 12 people to meet Transport Canada vessel capacity rules, and the centre's own sample itinerary for this length is built for 24 people including teachers and chaperones. Groups other than schools use the same program; the centre lists Girl Guides, Scouts, First Nations educational events and artist retreats among past visitors. Bursaries can be requested for a whole class or for individual students when you apply.
programs.what_children_do: They arrive by bus, check in at the Whale Lab, put their bags in a dorm room, then walk the campus on a safety orientation. In the labs they handle live invertebrates from Barkley Sound and hunt through a drop of seawater for plankton under a microscope. Outside they ride a skiff up Grappler Inlet to measure the water, dredge the sea floor from the Alta, shuttle across by boat and hike about twenty minutes to Brady's Beach to work the tide pools at low tide, and finish with a guided walk through the rainforest.
programs.our_note: This is a sleepover trip, not a day out. Children share bunk rooms, eat in the cafeteria and are on boats and slippery rock for a good part of each day, and boots and rain gear are on the centre's own packing list. Getting there is the real planning job, because the last stretch from Port Alberni is about 76 km of logging road with no gas and no cell service, and travel is not in the price. Ask about the bursaries early; they are offered for a whole class as well as for individual students, and they close before the trip season.
programs.practical_summary: Meals are cooked on site and eaten in a peanut free dining hall that handles most dietary needs, everyone sleeps in campus dorms, and there are washrooms and showers on each floor. How many adults have to come, whether chaperones pay the same, step free access and where a bus parks are not written down, and the price is quoted per group, so ask for a written quote before you apply.
programs.extra_fees_note: Final pricing is based on group size, accommodation requirements, season, and selected educational activities. Transportation to and from Bamfield is not included. Some activities that are offered through the Field Trip Program have an associated additional cost, including the Barkley Star boat trip and the Kiixin Village tour.

programs.name: Marine science field trip, 3 nights and 4 days
programs.description: A residential marine biology field trip on the BMSC campus. The published price includes accommodation, meals, instructional programming, laboratory and classroom facilities, and educational materials, and the site describes it as an estimated cost per person starting at $994. Final pricing is based on group size, accommodation requirements, season, and selected educational activities, and transport to and from Bamfield is not included. Bookings must be in multiples of 12 people to meet Transport Canada vessel capacity rules. The extra day makes room for longer activities such as the three to four hour intertidal trip to Brady's Beach, the Eagle Bay rocky shore, the experimental marine biology lab and the four hour Kiixin village tour led by a Huu-ay-aht guide, which carries an extra cost.
programs.what_children_do: They settle into a dorm room and then work as a small field crew for four days. In the labs they identify live invertebrates and seaweeds, keep a journal, and set up their own experiments with animals from the tanks. Outside they take water measurements from a skiff in Grappler Inlet, dredge the sea floor from the Alta, pick through tide pools at low tide on Brady's Beach and Eagle Bay, walk the old growth rainforest trail in boots, and go down to the dock after dark to look for bioluminescence.
programs.our_note: Four days is enough for the whole coastline to sink in, and it is also four nights of shared bunk rooms and full days outdoors in whatever weather arrives. The centre builds each itinerary with you, so send them the topics your group is already working on and they will try to fit activities around them. Two of the best trips, the fast boat around Barkley Sound and the Kiixin village tour, cost extra, so ask what they add before you agree to the itinerary.

programs.name: Marine science field trip, 4 nights and 5 days
programs.description: A residential marine biology field trip on the BMSC campus. The published price includes accommodation, meals, instructional programming, laboratory and classroom facilities, and educational materials, and the site describes it as an estimated cost per person starting at $1,275. Final pricing is based on group size, accommodation requirements, season, and selected educational activities, and transport to and from Bamfield is not included. Bookings must be in multiples of 12 people to meet Transport Canada vessel capacity rules. This is the only length that can include the Reproduction of Marine Invertebrates lab, where a culture of sea urchin or sand dollar embryos set up on the first day is checked for about ten minutes each following day.
programs.what_children_do: They live on campus for five days and move between the labs, the docks and the shoreline. They fertilise sea urchin eggs on the first day and come back each morning to watch the embryos change, identify seaweeds with a key, and design and run their own experiment with animals from the tanks before presenting what they found. Outside they crew a skiff for oceanography, dredge from the Alta, spend three or four hours in the tide pools at Brady's Beach, walk the rainforest trail, and make prints and cyanotypes from things they collected.
programs.our_note: Five days is a long way from home for a first residential trip, so it suits a group that has already slept away together. The embryo lab is the reason to pick this length over the shorter ones, because the daily checks only work if you are there for four nights. Boots and full rain gear matter more than anything else you pack; the centre's own advice is that the trail will be muddy and the weather is unpredictable.

gaps: no age or grade range is published for the field trips program, so ages here are unknown rather than open; their own pages give three different answers and this is recorded in conflicts
the per person prices are written as estimates starting at a figure, and the pricing page carries no year or season, so price_year_or_season is null and the real number comes from a quote
whether teachers and chaperones pay the same per person price is not stated anywhere
no maximum group size is published; bookings must be in multiples of 12 and the centre's own sample itinerary is built for 24 people including teachers and chaperones
no minimum group size is stated; 12 is the smallest possible multiple but the site never calls it a minimum
how many adults have to come is not stated anywhere on the site
no minimum notice or lead time is published; applications open twice a year for the fall and spring seasons, with bursary requests due on a separate earlier deadline
no deposit, payment timing or cancellation terms are published for field trips; the deposit and refund rules on the site are written for university course students, not for school groups
washrooms and showers are described for the dormitories in the housing PDF only, not for the laboratory and classroom buildings
step free or wheelchair access is not confirmed; the housing PDF asks groups with accessibility needs to contact the team first
bus parking is not described, although the sample itinerary has groups arriving at the centre by bus
no wet weather alternative is described for the beach, boat and rainforest activities
the site does not say whether children under five are welcome; the trip is residential and children sleep in shared bunk rooms
the homepage banner photographs are loaded by a slider script and do not appear in the page source, so the hero photo was taken from the facilities page instead

every photograph on the site carries an empty alt attribute, so all alt text here was written from the image file names and from where each photo sits on the page; no browser was available to look at the images themselves
months for the field trips program are taken from the published fall and spring seasons; the centre does not publish exact dates until each season is announced

values: We provide experiential field trips for high school and Undergraduate students.
We host field trips for learners of all ages
Classes from kindergarten up to grade 12 from BC and Alberta are eligible to apply.
conflicts.note: Their own pages do not agree on who these trips are for. One says high school and university students, another says learners of all ages, and the bursary page says classes from kindergarten to grade 12 can apply. Ask what they will actually take for your group's ages before you plan anything else.

Two of their pages give different costs. One says about $285 a person a night, the other starts at $713 a person for two nights and three days. We use the higher, newer one. Ask them for a written quote for your dates, because the final price depends on your group size and which activities you pick.
